title: [File Locksmith] ExplorerCommand::LaunchUI ignores CreateProcessW failure

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code change is plausible; uncertainty and confidence are stated in the proposed plan.

verification: Force/mock CreateProcessW failure; verify corresponding HRESULT and no invalid handle close.
Verify success still closes returned handles and reports success.

confidence.rationale: The source defect matches the report and the correction is localized and directly testable.

plan: On failure, capture GetLastError and return HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(error) without closing uninitialized handles.
On success close valid handles and preserve launch behavior.
proposed_fixes.title: Propagate File Locksmith UI launch failures
proposed_fixes.root_cause: ExplorerCommand::LaunchUI ignores CreateProcessW failure, then closes process handles and returns S_OK, hiding launch errors and risking invalid handle operations.

issue_context.analysis: The issue’s concrete defect is corroborated in the owning source. Check the BOOL result before touching PROCESS_INFORMATION handles and return HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(GetLastError()).
initial_investigation: Reviewed src/modules/FileLocksmith/FileLocksmithExt/ExplorerCommand.cpp around ExplorerCommand::LaunchUI; confirmed unchecked CreateProcessW and unconditional handle close / S_OK return.
inferences: When process creation fails, current code may access invalid handles and suppress the Win32 failure.
known_information: The report pinpoints CreateProcessW in File Locksmith ExplorerCommand::LaunchUI.
Source review confirms the process creation result is ignored and handle closing / success return are unconditional.
issue_context.summary: File Locksmith can report success when ExplorerCommand fails to launch its UI, and may close handles that were never initialized.
